denial.reason_text: Insufficient documentation of prior treatment failure. The information we received does not show that the member completed a trial of a preferred oral preventive medication, or that the trial was ineffective or not tolerated.

requirements.text: Migraine diagnosis with at least 4 migraine days monthly for prior 3 months
requirements.policy_text: The member has a diagnosis of migraine with at least 4 migraine days per month in each of the 3 months before the request.

evidence.quote: Headache diary for June through August 2026: 7 migraine days in June, 8 in July, and 9 in August.
evidence.rationale: The neurologist's diary review gives migraine-day counts for each of the three months (June, July, August 2026) before the 09/15/2026 prior authorization submission.
The neurologist documents a migraine diagnosis with an ICD-10 code in the consultation assessment.

near_misses.quote: Headache diary reviewed for March through May 2026: 9 migraine days in March, 8 in April, and 10 in May.
near_misses.why_not: These counts cover March to May 2026, which is not the three months immediately before the request.

near_misses.quote: Migraine frequency was unchanged, with 8 migraine days in July.
near_misses.why_not: It gives only one month (July), so it cannot show the count for each of the three months by itself.
This is a provisional primary-care impression ('probable'), not a confirmed diagnosis, and it gives no migraine-day counts.

quantity_check.label: migraine days per month in each of the 3 months before the request

requirements.text: Completed at least 8 weeks on a preferred oral preventive
requirements.policy_text: The member completed a trial of at least 8 weeks of at least one preferred oral preventive medication.

evidence.quote: Patient completed an eight-week trial of topiramate, 06/08/2026 to 08/03/2026.
evidence.rationale: The treating neurologist documents a completed trial of oral topiramate lasting eight weeks, with start and stop dates that span 8 weeks.

near_misses.why_not: This is an interim status at the 07/06/2026 visit, with only four weeks completed. The full trial duration is documented on the later 08/03/2026 note.

near_misses.quote: Start topiramate 25 mg nightly today, 06/08/2026, increasing by 25 mg each week to a target of 50 mg twice daily.
near_misses.why_not: This is a plan to start treatment, not evidence that any duration was completed.

near_misses.quote: Amitriptyline 10 mg nightly was prescribed in 2023 for insomnia; she took it for about 2 weeks and stopped because of morning grogginess.
near_misses.why_not: This was a brief 2023 course of a different drug, prescribed for insomnia rather than migraine prevention, and it lasted about 2 weeks.

quantity_check.label: duration of preferred oral preventive trial

requirements.text: Trial was ineffective or stopped for intolerable adverse effects
requirements.policy_text: The trial in (b) was ineffective or was discontinued because of intolerable adverse effects.

evidence.quote: Patient completed an eight-week trial of topiramate, 06/08/2026 to 08/03/2026. Treatment was discontinued today due to significant nausea and dizziness, which were not tolerable despite dose adjustment.

key_phrases.text: discontinued today due to significant nausea and dizziness

evidence.rationale: The neurologist explicitly documents that the topiramate trial was stopped because of intolerable nausea and dizziness after an eight-week course.

evidence.quote: Episodic migraine without aura, inadequately controlled. Topiramate stopped because of intolerance.
evidence.rationale: The assessment states the topiramate was stopped for intolerance and the migraine remained inadequately controlled.

near_misses.quote: Migraine frequency not yet improved; adverse effects present.
near_misses.why_not: This is a mid-trial note and the plan was to continue treatment, so it does not show the trial failed or was discontinued.

near_misses.quote: Nausea continues on the adjusted dose and she feels dizzy when standing up quickly.
near_misses.why_not: This is a nurse's telephone record of the patient's symptoms while she was still advised to continue the drug, not a clinician's determination of failure or intolerance.

near_misses.quote: Amitriptyline 10 mg nightly was prescribed in 2023 for insomnia; she took it for about 2 weeks and stopped because of morning grogginess.
near_misses.why_not: This describes a different drug, taken in 2023 for insomnia rather than migraine prevention, so it is not the trial in question.

requirements.text: Prescribed by or with a neurologist or headache specialist
requirements.policy_text: The medication is prescribed by, or in consultation with, a neurologist or headache specialist.

evidence.quote: Erenumab-aooe 70 mg subcutaneously once monthly - ordered by Elena M. Castellanos, MD (Neurology); pending prior authorization.

key_phrases.text: ordered by Elena M. Castellanos, MD

evidence.rationale: The medication list states that the erenumab-aooe order was placed by Dr. Castellanos, whose specialty is given as Neurology.

near_misses.quote: Probable migraine without aura. Referral placed to neurology.
near_misses.why_not: This is a primary care referral to neurology. It does not show that a neurologist prescribed or was consulted on the requested medication.

blocks.text: Re: Appeal of denial dated 2026-09-22, Case A-2048, Alderpoint Health Plan, request for Erenumab-aooe 70 mg subcutaneous injection, once monthly, 12 months

We are writing to request reconsideration of this denial. This appeal is made under the initial authorization criteria in section 3.1 of policy MP-RX-014, and it responds to the stated reason that prior treatment failure was not sufficiently documented.
The record documents a headache diary for June through August 2026 showing 7 migraine days in June, 8 in July, and 9 in August, with a diagnosis of episodic migraine without aura.
The record documents that the patient completed an eight-week trial of topiramate, 06/08/2026 to 08/03/2026.
The record documents that topiramate was discontinued because of significant nausea and dizziness that were not tolerable despite dose adjustment, and that the migraine was inadequately controlled.
The record documents that erenumab-aooe 70 mg subcutaneously once monthly was ordered by Elena M. Castellanos, MD (Neurology).
Thank you for your time. We ask that the plan review the enclosed documentation and reconsider its determination. Please contact our office if any further information is needed.
